chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from someone else from our companions, said:

We said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! (Supposing) we are not able upon the (palm) twigs?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A lotus twig'. It was said, 'Supposing we are not able upon the lotus?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A different twig'.

key_terms.السِّدْر: Lotus wood (from the Sidr tree), a preferred material for prayer mats
key_terms.الْجَرِيدَة: Palm twigs or strips of palm wood, traditionally used for prayer mats
key_terms.الْخِلَاف: Other/different wood, used as a fallback when preferred materials are unavailable

ai.seo_question: What are the preferred materials for a prayer mat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes a pragmatic hierarchy for the *musalla* (prayer mat), prioritizing palm twigs (*jaridah*) and lotus wood (*sidr*) before allowing any other wood (*khalaf*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on using natural, pure materials for prostration. It underscores the principle of *takhayyur* (choice) within the bounds of reverence, ensuring that even in scarcity, the act of prayer remains dignified and connected to the earth. This ruling is often cited by jurists to demonstrate the flexibility of ritual purity laws when specific preferred items are inaccessible.
